claim: EMT is a cellular process that converts epithelial cells to mesenchymal cells with migratory potential.
source: Epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a cellular process that converts epithelial cells to mesenchymal cells with migratory potential (Hay, 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hay, 1995, which is a reference to established scientific literature.

claim: EMT plays an essential role in embryonic morphogenesis, wound healing, tissue fibrosis, and cancer progression.
source: EMT plays an essential role in various developmental and pathological processes such as embryonic morphogenesis, wound healing, tissue fibrosis, and cancer progression (Zhao and Trainor, 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhao and Trainor, 2023.

claim: Studies of EMT have increased exponentially in the past 5 years due to the implied role of EMT in cancer malignancy.
source: Studies of EMT, particularly in the field of cancer biology, have increased exponentially in the past 5 years due to the implied role of EMT in numerous aspects of malignancy such as cancer cell invasion, survival, stemness, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and tumor heterogeneity (Yang et al., 2020a).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yang et al., 2020a.

claim: EMT has traditionally been considered a binary process comprising either full epithelial cell or mesenchymal cell states.
source: EMT has traditionally been considered a binary process comprising either full epithelial cell or mesenchymal cell states.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus about how EMT was historically viewed.

claim: Studies of cancer have uncovered epithelial to mesenchymal plasticity (EMP), in which multiple intermediate states exist along the EMT spectrum.
source: However, studies of cancer have uncovered an alternative scenario termed epithelial to mesenchymal plasticity (EMP), in which multiple intermediate states exist along the EMT spectrum (Dong et al., 2018; Gonzalez et al., 2018; Huang et al., 2013; Karacosta et al., 2019; Kumar et al., 2019; Pastushenko et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to cancer studies.

claim: In head and neck cancer, primary tumors and matching lymph nodes contain a subpopulation of tumor cells in a partial EMT state expressing both epithelial and mesenchymal marker genes.
source: More specifically, in some cases of head and neck cancer, primary tumors and matching lymph nodes contain a subpopulation of tumor cells in a partial EMT state, as defined by their expression of both epithelial marker genes and mesenchymal marker genes (Puram et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Puram et al., 2017.

claim: Cells in partial EMT state are highly invasive and located at the leading edge of tumors in vivo.
source: Moreover, cells in this partial EMT state are highly invasive and located at the leading edge of tumors in vivo.
evidence: This claim is presented as a finding from the previously cited cancer studies.

claim: In mouse xenograft models of skin cancer and breast cancer, early EMT hybrid states expressed both Vimentin and Cytokeratin 14 at intermediate levels and had high metastatic potential.
source: Similarly, in mouse xenograft models of skin cancer and breast cancer, the absence of epithelial cellular adhesion molecules in several cell populations was discovered to represent early EMT hybrid states as they also expressed both Vimentin and Cytokeratin 14 at intermediate levels and consequently had high metastatic potential (Pastushenko et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pastushenko et al., 2018.

claim: Partial EMT states have been recognized in lung cancer and ovarian cancer.
source: Partial EMT states have also been recognized in lung cancer and ovarian cancer (Gonzalez et al., 2018; Karacosta et al., 2019), with tumor cells expressing both the epithelial marker E-cadherin and the mesenchymal marker Vimentin.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gonzalez et al., 2018 and Karacosta et al., 2019.

claim: EMT intermediate states have been identified in circulating tumor cells from patient samples.
source: Besides primary tumors, EMT intermediate states have also been identified in circulating tumor cells from patient samples (Yu et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yu et al., 2013.

claim: EMT during embryogenesis and cancer progression share analogous phenotypic changes involving similar core transcription factors and molecular mechanisms.
source: Since EMT during embryogenesis and cancer progression have been shown to share analogous phenotypic changes that involve similar core transcription factors and molecular mechanisms, it was proposed that the initiation and development of carcinoma could be attributed to an unusual activation of EMT factors involved in normal developmental processes (Hay, 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hay, 1995.

claim: It remains largely unknown whether intermediate or transition states exist or play a role in classic developmental EMT.
source: However, compared to tumorigenesis, it remains largely unknown whether intermediate or transition states exist or play a role in classic developmental EMT.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: NCC formation is a classic example of developmental EMT.
source: NCC formation is a classic example of developmental EMT (Lee et al., 2013; Zhao and Trainor, 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2013 and Zhao and Trainor, 2023.

claim: NCC are a migratory progenitor cell population unique to vertebrates.
source: NCC are a migratory progenitor cell population unique to vertebrates.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about NCC.

claim: NCC are formed during neurulation in the dorsolateral domain of the neural plate.
source: Formed during neurulation in the dorsolateral domain of the neural plate, EMT facilitates their delamination from the neuroepithelium and migration throughout the body, where they differentiate into neurons and glia of the peripheral nervous system, pigment cells in the skin, craniofacial bone and cartilage, as well as many other cell types (Bhatt et al., 2013; Dash and Trainor, 2020; Lièvre and Douarin, 1975; Trainor, 2005; Weston, 1983).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: NCC differentiate into neurons and glia of the peripheral nervous system, pigment cells in the skin, craniofacial bone and cartilage, and many other cell types.
source: Formed during neurulation in the dorsolateral domain of the neural plate, EMT facilitates their delamination from the neuroepithelium and migration throughout the body, where they differentiate into neurons and glia of the peripheral nervous system, pigment cells in the skin, craniofacial bone and cartilage, as well as many other cell types (Bhatt et al., 2013; Dash and Trainor, 2020; Lièvre and Douarin, 1975; Trainor, 2005; Weston, 1983).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Disruption of NCC delamination and migration can result in developmental abnormalities referred to as neurocristopathies.
source: Disruption of NCC delamination and migration can result in developmental abnormalities, referred to as neurocristopathies (Achilleos and Trainor, 2015; Watt and Trainor, 2014), hence it is important to study the mechanisms that regulate mammalian NCC development.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Achilleos and Trainor, 2015 and Watt and Trainor, 2014.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify and define intermediate transcriptional and cellular states during mouse cranial NCC EMT and delamination.
source: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to identify and define intermediate transcriptional and cellular states during mouse cranial NCC EMT and delamination.
evidence: This is a statement of the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Two NCC EMT intermediate populations were identified distinguished by their S or G2/M cell cycle phase state during delamination.
source: We identified two NCC EMT intermediate populations distinguished by their S or G2/M cell cycle phase state during delamination.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the scRNA-seq analysis presented in the study.

claim: Trajectory analyses reveal that the distinct intermediate populations are formed simultaneously and independently but then converge into a single or common pool.
source: Interestingly, trajectory analyses reveal that these distinct intermediate populations are formed simultaneously, and independently, but then converge into a single or common pool, suggesting they do not have distinct fates following migration.
evidence: This is a finding from the trajectory analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The convergence of intermediate populations into a common pool is consistent with the known plasticity and potency of early migrating NCC.
source: This is consistent with the known plasticity and potency of early migrating NCC (Golding et al., 2000; Sandell and Trainor, 2006; Trainor and Krumlauf, 2000a; Trainor and Krumlauf, 2000b; Trainor and Krumlauf, 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies on NCC plasticity.

claim: The intermediate NCC populations are defined by unique transcriptional signatures, including differential expression of genes involved in cell protrusion such as Dlc1, Pak3, and Sp5.
source: Transcriptional profiling revealed that the intermediate NCC populations could also be defined by unique transcriptional signatures, including differential expression of genes involved in cell protrusion, such as Dlc1, Pak3, and Sp5.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptional profiling analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: SABER-FISH revealed that intermediate NCC populations were spatially localized in the dorsolateral region of the neural plate.
source: Further interrogation using signal amplification by exchange reaction for multiplexed fluorescent in situ hybridization (SABER-FISH) revealed that these intermediate NCC populations were spatially localized in the dorsolateral region of the neural plate.
evidence: This is a finding from the SABER-FISH experiments.

claim: Knocking down Dlc1 led to a significant reduction in the number of migratory NCC.
source: In addition, knocking down the NCC EMT intermediate marker Dlc1 led to a significant reduction in the number of migratory NCC, which revealed a critical role for Dlc1 in the regulation of mouse cranial NCC delamination.
evidence: This is a finding from the Dlc1 knockdown experiments.

claim: Dlc1 plays a critical role in the regulation of mouse cranial NCC delamination.
source: In addition, knocking down the NCC EMT intermediate marker Dlc1 led to a significant reduction in the number of migratory NCC, which revealed a critical role for Dlc1 in the regulation of mouse cranial NCC delamination.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Dlc1 knockdown experimental results.

claim: The final scRNA-seq dataset consisted of 21,190 cells (12,498 cells from Wnt1-Cre;RosaLSL-eYFP and 8,692 from Mef2c-F10N-LacZ) and 29,041 genes.
source: The final dataset used for analysis consisted of 21,190 cells (12,498 cells from Wnt1-Cre;RosaLSL-eYFP and 8692 from Mef2c-F10N-LacZ) and 29,041 genes.
evidence: This information is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In E8.5 Wnt1-Cre;RosaLSL-eYFP embryos, YFP is expressed by Wnt1+ neuroepithelial cells located in the dorsolateral neural plate.
source: In E8.5 Wnt1-Cre;RosaLSL-eYFP embryos, YFP is expressed by Wnt1+ neuroepithelial cells located in the dorsolateral neural plate, which encompasses premigratory NCC (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Wnt1-Cre;RosaLSL-eYFP labels premigratory and migratory NCC and other lineage labeled cells derived from the Wnt1+ cell population.
source: Consequently, Wnt1-Cre;RosaLSL-eYFP labels premigratory and migratory NCC and other lineage labeled cells derived from the Wnt1+ cell population (Figure 1B; Chai et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mef2c-F10N-LacZ predominantly labels migratory NCC, with LacZ activity driven by the F10N enhancer of the Mef2c gene.
source: In contrast, Mef2c-F10N-LacZ predominantly labels migratory NCC, with LacZ activity driven by the F10N enhancer of the Mef2c gene (Figure 1B; Aoto et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Six major cell or tissue types were identified in E8.5 mouse embryonic cranial tissues: cranial NCC, neuroectoderm, non-neural ectoderm, mesoderm, endothelial cells, and embryonic blood cells.
source: We initially identified six major cell or tissue types present in E8.5 mouse embryonic cranial tissues based on the differential expression of classic cell or tissue type-specific markers, and we clustered the data accordingly (Figure 1C and D; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Sox1 and Sox2 were used to delineate neural ectoderm.
source: For example, Sox1 and Sox2 were used to delineate neural ectoderm, whereas Cdh1 (E-cadherin) was used to define non-neural ectoderm.
evidence: This is stated as part of the methodology for identifying cell types.

claim: Cdh1 (E-cadherin) was used to define non-neural ectoderm.
source: For example, Sox1 and Sox2 were used to delineate neural ectoderm, whereas Cdh1 (E-cadherin) was used to define non-neural ectoderm.
evidence: This is stated as part of the methodology for identifying cell types.

claim: eYFP, LacZ, Sox10, and Twist delineated migrating NCC.
source: eYFP, LacZ, Sox10, and Twist delineated migrating NCC.
evidence: This is stated as part of the methodology for identifying cell types.

claim: Tbx1 was primarily used as a marker of mesoderm cells.
source: Tbx1 was primarily used as a marker of mesoderm cells and Kdr (Vegfr2) demarcated mesoderm-derived endothelial cells.
evidence: This is stated as part of the methodology for identifying cell types.

claim: Kdr (Vegfr2) demarcated mesoderm-derived endothelial cells.
source: Tbx1 was primarily used as a marker of mesoderm cells and Kdr (Vegfr2) demarcated mesoderm-derived endothelial cells.
evidence: This is stated as part of the methodology for identifying cell types.

claim: The cranial NCC cluster was divided into five subclusters at a resolution of 0.26.
source: We then bioinformatically segregated the cranial NCC cluster, which includes both premigratory and migratory NCC, and divided it into five subclusters at a resolution of 0.26 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A high percentage of cells in subclusters 0–3 express elevated levels of markers of migratory NCC (Vim, Sox10, Twist1).
source: A high percentage of cells in subclusters 0–3 express elevated levels of markers of migratory NCC (Vim, Sox10, Twist1), while only subclusters 0 and 1 exhibit high levels of expression of NCC specifier genes (Zeb2, Pax3, Nr6a1, Sox9, Foxd3, Snai1) (Figure 2B; Cheung et al., 2005; Dottori et al., 2001; Hari et al., 2012; Kobayashi et al., 2020; Lee et al., 2013; Li et al., 2000; Murdoch et al., 2012; Schorle et al., 1996; Soo et al., 2002; Van de Putte et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Only subclusters 0 and 1 exhibit high levels of expression of NCC specifier genes (Zeb2, Pax3, Nr6a1, Sox9, Foxd3, Snai1).
source: A high percentage of cells in subclusters 0–3 express elevated levels of markers of migratory NCC (Vim, Sox10, Twist1), while only subclusters 0 and 1 exhibit high levels of expression of NCC specifier genes (Zeb2, Pax3, Nr6a1, Sox9, Foxd3, Snai1) (Figure 2B; Cheung et al., 2005; Dottori et al., 2001; Hari et al., 2012; Kobayashi et al., 2020; Lee et al., 2013; Li et al., 2000; Murdoch et al., 2012; Schorle et al., 1996; Soo et al., 2002; Van de Putte et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Subclusters 0 and 1 likely represent an earlier stage of NCC delamination and migration than subclusters 2 and 3.
source: Since NCC specifiers are downregulated as NCC migrate and later differentiate into specific lineages, the combinatorial expression of genes suggests that subclusters 0 and 1 likely represent an earlier stage of NCC delamination and migration than subclusters 2 and 3.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression patterns observed in the data.

claim: Subclusters 0 and 1 contain early migratory NCC, whereas subclusters 2 and 3 comprise late migratory NCC.
source: Furthermore, subclusters 2 and 3 express a significantly higher level of late migratory NCC program genes than subclusters 0 and 1, which demonstrates that subclusters 0 and 1 contain early migratory NCC, whereas subclusters 2 and 3 comprise late migratory NCC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Subcluster 0 might also contain premigratory NCC that do not yet express any migratory NCC genes.
source: Interestingly, we also observed that a small percentage of subcluster 0 cells express early migratory NCC genes, but at a lower intensity compared to subcluster 1. This implies that subcluster 0 might also contain premigratory NCC that do not yet express any migratory NCC genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression patterns observed in the data.

claim: Subcluster 2 displays a high level of expression of pharyngeal arch NCC mesenchyme marker Dlx2.
source: More specifically, subcluster 2 displays a high level of expression of pharyngeal arch NCC mesenchyme marker Dlx2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Bulfone et al., 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Subcluster 3 expresses a frontonasal mesenchyme marker Alx1.
source: In contrast, subcluster 3 expresses a frontonasal mesenchyme marker Alx1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Iyyanar et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Subcluster 4 exhibits higher expression of Sox1 and Sox2 indicative of a neuroepithelial identity.
source: Subcluster 4 exhibits a unique transcriptional profile distinct from subclusters 0–3 (Figure 2B). Higher expression of Sox1 and Sox2 is indicative of a neuroepithelial identity for subcluster 4 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: During NCC formation, Sox1 and Sox2 are downregulated in the dorsal neural plate border domain but remain strongly expressed more ventrally throughout the neural plate.
source: During NCC formation, Sox1 and Sox2 are downregulated in the dorsal neural plate border domain but remain strongly expressed more ventrally throughout the neural plate (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about NCC formation.

claim: Sox9 and Sox10 are activated during NCC formation in what is known as the SoxB (1/2) to SoxE (9/10) switch.
source: Concomitantly, Sox9 and Sox10 are activated in what is known as the SoxB (1/2) to SoxE (9/10) switch (Mandalos et al., 2014; Remboutsika et al., 2011; Wakamatsu et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: Overexpressing Sox2 in the dorsal neural tube represses NCC specification.
source: Consistent with this model, overexpressing Sox2 in the dorsal neural tube has been shown to repress NCC specification, whereas overexpressing Sox9 and Sox10 have been shown to precociously promote NCC formation (Aybar et al., 2003; Cheung and Briscoe, 2003; Mandalos et al., 2014; McKeown et al., 2005; Remboutsika et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: Overexpressing Sox9 and Sox10 precociously promote NCC formation.
source: Consistent with this model, overexpressing Sox2 in the dorsal neural tube has been shown to repress NCC specification, whereas overexpressing Sox9 and Sox10 have been shown to precociously promote NCC formation (Aybar et al., 2003; Cheung and Briscoe, 2003; Mandalos et al., 2014; McKeown et al., 2005; Remboutsika et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous studies.

claim: Subcluster 17' comprises premigratory NCC.
source: The heatmap shows that a significant number of cells in subcluster 17' express a much higher level of Wnt1 than any other subcluster, suggesting that subcluster 17' comprises premigratory NCC (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression patterns shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Subcluster 17' cells express neural plate border and NCC specifier genes such as Zic2, Pax7, Nr6a1, Pax3, Sox9, and Foxd3, but do not express migratory NCC markers such as Sox10 and Vim.
source: Consistent with this observation, subcluster 17' cells also express other neural plate border and NCC specifier genes such as Zic2, Pax7, Nr6a1, Pax3, Sox9, and Foxd3, but does not express migratory NCC markers such as Sox10 and Vim (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Subclusters 2' and 10' could represent EMT intermediate states as premigratory NCC transition to migratory NCC during delamination.
source: Subclusters 2' and 10' share a similar expression profile to subcluster 17'. However, subclusters 2' and 10' express less Wnt1 and less neural plate border specifiers such as Zic2 and Pax7 than subcluster 17' (Figure 2D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1). This data suggests that subclusters 2' and 10' could represent EMT intermediate states as premigratory NCC transition to migratory NCC during delamination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene expression patterns shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Intermediate NCC exhibit a decrease in Nectin, Cadherin, and Tight Junction Protein gene expression consistent with intercellular tight junction breakdown and degradation of apicobasal polarity.
source: Intermediate NCC exhibit a decrease in Nectin (e.g. Nectin, 1, Nectin2, Nectin3), Cadherin (e.g. Cadh2, Cadh6, Cadh11), and Tight Junction Protein (e.g. Cldna1, TJp1, TJP2) gene expression consistent with intercellular tight junction breakdown and degradation of apicobasal polarity (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Subcluster 2 and 10 cells exhibit an increase in Rac, Rack1, and Cdc42 gene expression which is indicative of cytoskeletal rearrangement and the formation of cell protrusions.
source: At the same time, subcluster 2 and 10 cells exhibit an increase in Rac, Rack1, and Cdc42 gene expression which is indicative of cytoskeletal rearrangement and the formation of cell protrusions (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: NCC in subcluster 2' primarily express S phase cell cycle genes such as Pcna, Pol1 subunits, Plk1, Ccnd, and Mcm family members.
source: NCC in subcluster 2' primarily express S phase cell cycle genes such as Pcna, Pol1 subunits, Plk1, Ccnd, and Mcm family members.
evidence: This is stated in the text based on analysis of gene expression data.

claim: NCC in subcluster 10' predominantly express G2/M phase cell cycle genes including Mik67, Aurka/b, Cenp, and Kif family members.
source: In contrast, NCC in subcluster 10' predominantly express G2/M phase cell cycle genes including Mik67, Aurka/b, Cenp, and Kif family members (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Premigratory and EMT intermediate NCC were identified as the earliest discrete populations to form among the entire cranial NCC population.
source: Premigratory and EMT intermediate NCC were identified as the earliest discrete populations to form among the entire cranial NCC population (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C based on pseudotime analysis.

claim: Late migratory NCC represent a more mature stage of NCC development.
source: In contrast, late migratory NCC represent a more mature stage of NCC development (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C based on pseudotime analysis.

claim: NCC can arise through two independent paths and initially become two distinct intermediate populations (subclusters 2' and 10') during EMT.
source: The trajectory analysis also demonstrates that NCC can arise through two independent paths and initially become two distinct intermediate populations (subclusters 2' and 10') during EMT (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3D based on trajectory analysis.

claim: The trajectories or lineages of the intermediate NCC subclusters merge back together into a single or common population of early migratory NCC.
source: Later the trajectories or lineages of the intermediate NCC subclusters then merge back together into a single or common population of early migratory NCC, before ultimately maturing into still as yet undifferentiated late migratory NCC as they colonize the frontonasal or pharyngeal arch mesenchyme (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3D based on trajectory analysis.

claim: Premigratory NCC can undergo EMT and delamination in either S phase or G2/M phase of the cell cycle.
source: Moreover, the different cell cycle status of subclusters 2' and 10' suggest that premigratory NCC can undergo EMT and delamination in either S phase or G2/M phase of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cell cycle gene expression patterns and trajectory analysis.

claim: EMT intermediate NCC and their immediate lineages are not fate restricted to any specific cranial NCC derivative at this timepoint.
source: The trajectory analysis further depicts that EMT intermediate NCC and their immediate lineages are not fate restricted to any specific cranial NCC derivative at this timepoint.
evidence: This is an inference based on the trajectory analysis results.

claim: A majority of delaminating cranial NCC express either EdU or pHH3 or both.
source: A majority of delaminating cranial NCC express either EdU or pHH3 or both. Only a very small percentage of cells do not express either of these cell cycle markers (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4C based on immunostaining experiments.

claim: Almost 50% of premigratory, non-delaminating trunk NCC in the dorsolateral neural tube do not express either EdU or pHH3 cell cycle markers.
source: In contrast, almost 50% of premigratory, non-delaminating trunk NCC in the dorsolateral neural tube do not express either cell cycle marker (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4D based on immunostaining experiments.

claim: Specific cell cycle phases are intimately connected to mouse cranial NCC EMT and delamination.
source: These observations imply that specific cell cycle phases are intimately connected to mouse cranial NCC EMT and delamination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cell cycle marker staining results.

claim: Aphidicolin treatment prevented cells from entering S phase cell cycle and induced minimal cell death.
source: Aphidicolin treatment in early E8.5 CD1 embryos for 12–13 hr prevented cells from entering S phase cell cycle and induced minimal cell death. Aphidicolin-treated embryos exhibit a lack of EdU incorporation and a similar level of TUNEL signal compared to the control.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Aphidicolin-treated embryos exhibit significantly fewer migratory NCC in the craniofacial region compared to DMSO-treated control embryos.
source: Quantification of Sox10 positive cells revealed significantly fewer migratory NCC in the craniofacial region of Aphidicolin-treated embryos compared to DMSO-treated control embryos (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4E based on quantification of immunostaining.

claim: pHH3 is expressed by a major proportion of the remaining migratory NCC after Aphidicolin treatment.
source: Interestingly, pHH3 is expressed by a major proportion of the remaining migratory NCC after Aphidicolin treatment (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4B based on immunostaining.

claim: Cranial NCC delamination in G2/M phase of the cell cycle (subcluster 10' NCC) is independent of delamination in S phase of the cell cycle (subcluster 2' NCC).
source: This data is consistent with the pseudotime trajectory analysis that cranial NCC delamination in G2/M phase of the cell cycle (subcluster 10' NCC) is independent of delamination in S phase of the cell cycle (subcluster 2' NCC).
evidence: This is an inference based on the Aphidicolin treatment results and trajectory analysis.

claim: Cell cycle regulation is critical for cranial NCC delamination in mouse embryos.
source: Thus, our data shows that cranial NCC delamination is disrupted upon S phase cell cycle inhibition, which supports the hypothesis that cell cycle regulation is critical for cranial NCC delamination in mouse embryos.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Aphidicolin treatment experimental results.

claim: During cranial NCC development, Sp5 and Pak3 are expressed at high levels in both premigratory and intermediate stage NCC.
source: During cranial NCC development, Sp5 and Pak3 are expressed at high levels in both premigratory and intermediate stage NCC.
evidence: This is stated based on analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Dlc1 is highly expressed in intermediate and migratory NCC.
source: In contrast, Dlc1 is highly expressed in intermediate and migratory NCC (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A based on scRNA-seq data.

claim: Wnt1 is expressed in the neuroepithelium and Sox10 is expressed in migratory NCC populating the underlying mesenchyme.
source: Higher magnification insets of the left side neural fold (box) showing that Wnt1 is expressed in the neuroepithelium and Sox10 is expressed in migratory NCC populating the underlying mesenchyme.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5B based on SABER-FISH staining.

claim: Dlc1, Sp5, and Pak3 are expressed in the dorsolateral most region of the neuroepithelium.
source: Dlc1, Sp5, and Pak3 are expressed in the dorsolateral most region of the neuroepithelium.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5B based on SABER-FISH staining.

claim: In the most dorsolateral domain where Wnt1 expression is slightly diminished, the intermediate stage NCC markers Dlc1, Sp5, and Pak3 are highly expressed.
source: However, in the most dorsolateral domain, where Wnt1 expression is slightly diminished, the intermediate stage NCC markers Dlc1, Sp5, and Pak3 are highly expressed (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5C based on polyline kymograph analysis of SABER-FISH data.

claim: Minimal Sox10 expression is detected in the transition region at the edge of the neuroepithelium.
source: In contrast, minimal Sox10 expression is detected in this transition region at the edge of the neuroepithelium, but high levels of Sox10 in the clear absence of Wnt1, Dlc1, Sp5, and Pak3, is observed in migratory NCC located more ventrally (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5C based on polyline kymograph analysis of SABER-FISH data.

claim: EMT intermediate stages can be transcriptionally defined and spatially resolved to the dorsolateral most region of the neuroepithelium.
source: Therefore, our data indicates that EMT intermediate stages can not only be transcriptionally defined, but also spatially resolved to the dorsolateral most region of the neuroepithelium.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the SABER-FISH experimental results.

claim: Dlc1 is not expressed by premigratory NCC but is expressed at high levels in all EMT intermediate stage NCC.
source: We prioritized Dlc1 over Pak3 and Sp5 because Dlc1 is not expressed by premigratory NCC but is expressed at high levels in all EMT intermediate stage NCC.
evidence: This is stated as the rationale for prioritizing Dlc1 for functional studies.

claim: Dlc1 null mutant mice are embryonically lethal and exhibit craniofacial malformation phenotypes.
source: Furthermore, Dlc1 null mutant mice are embryonically lethal and exhibit craniofacial malformation phenotypes (Sabbir et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Sabbir et al., 2010.

claim: E10.5 Dlc1 null mouse embryos exhibit hyperplastic frontonasal prominences and pharyngeal arches, a neural tube closure defect and underdeveloped atrial and ventricular walls of the heart.
source: Specifically, gross morphological anomalies of craniofacial tissues such as frontonasal prominence and pharyngeal arch hypoplasia are apparent in E10.5 Dlc1 null mouse embryos, which is suggestive of a perturbation of NCC development (Sabbir et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Sabbir et al., 2010.

claim: Pak3 and Sp5 null mutant mice are healthy and fertile with no obvious abnormalities.
source: Moreover, Pak3 and Sp5 null mutant mice are healthy and fertile with no obvious abnormalities.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about these mutant mice.

claim: The number of migratory NCC was significantly reduced in all Dlc1 knockdown embryos.
source: We subsequently observed that the number of migratory NCC was significantly reduced in all Dlc1 knockdown embryos (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6B based on Sox10 immunostaining quantification.

claim: Each of the Dlc1 shRNA constructs led to a significant reduction in the number of migratory NCC compared to their respective control.
source: In fact, each of the Dlc1 shRNA constructs led to a significant reduction in the number of migratory NCC compared to their respective control (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: No difference in cell death was observed in Dlc1 knockdown embryos comparable to controls.
source: Importantly, we did not observe any difference in cell death in Dlc1 knockdown embryos comparable to controls (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6D based on TUNEL staining.

claim: An average of 30% reduction of Dlc1 expression was achieved by each Dlc1 shRNA lentivirus knockdown.
source: On average, a 30% reduction of Dlc1 expression was achieved by each Dlc1 shRNA lentivirus knockdown (Figure 6C; Figure 6—figure supplement 1), and notably, the Dlc1 isoforms targeted by the different Dlc1 shRNA constructs used in this study suggest a correlation with Dlc1 null mouse embryos and their phenotypes.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1 based on qRT-PCR analysis.

claim: Dlc1 is a Rho GTPase-activating protein (GAP) that regulates the activity of Rho family GTPases Rho and Cdc42.
source: Dlc1 is a Rho GTPase-activating protein (GAP) that regulates the activity of Rho family GTPases Rho and Cdc42 (Kim et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Kim et al., 2008.

claim: RhoGTPases regulate cell morphology and motility through modulating the activity of the actin cytoskeleton.
source: RhoGTPases are known to regulate cell morphology and motility through modulating the activity of the actin cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about RhoGTPases.

claim: Rho facilitates the formation of stress fibers.
source: More specifically, Rho has been shown to facilitate the formation of stress fibers, while Cdc42 is involved in filopodium formation (Kim et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Kim et al., 2008.

claim: Cdc42 is involved in filopodium formation.
source: More specifically, Rho has been shown to facilitate the formation of stress fibers, while Cdc42 is involved in filopodium formation (Kim et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Kim et al., 2008.

claim: RhoGTPases regulate the organization of tight junctions, which breakdown during EMT.
source: RhoGTPases also regulate the organization of tight junctions, which breakdown during EMT (Popoff and Geny, 2009; Terry et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Popoff and Geny, 2009 and Terry et al., 2010.

claim: The effect of Dlc1 knockdown on cranial NCC EMT and delamination may be mediated via disrupted RhoGTPase activity and subsequent downstream cellular changes.

source: In chicken embryos, Dlc1 overexpression results in ectopic trunk NCC delamination, including apically into the neural tube lumen, due to a disruption in apical-basal polarity of dorsal neuroepithelial cells (Liu et al., 2017).

claim: NCC overexpressing Dlc1 exhibit a loss of directionality during migration.

source: In addition, the downregulation of Dlc1 in migrating NCC restricts their motility.

claim: Dlc1 regulates trunk NCC delamination and migration in chicken embryos.
source: Thus, Dlc1 regulates trunk NCC delamination and migration in chicken embryos.

claim: In zebrafish embryos, Arhgap modulates NCC EMT and delamination via the localization of Rho activation to designated subcellular compartments in concert with promoting localized actomyosin contraction to trigger directional cell motility.
source: Interestingly, in zebrafish embryos, another GAP family member Arhgap has been shown to modulate NCC EMT and delamination via the localization of Rho activation to designated subcellular compartments in concert with promoting localized actomyosin contraction to trigger directional cell motility (Clay and Halloran, 2013).

claim: The knockdown of Arhgap in NCC results in Rho activation, which in turn inhibits NCC EMT and delamination.
source: More specifically, the knockdown of Arhgap in NCC results in Rho activation, which in turn inhibits NCC EMT and delamination.

claim: The role of Dlc1 during NCC delamination might be evolutionarily conserved in vertebrate embryos.
source: These data suggest that the role of Dlc1 during NCC delamination might be evolutionarily conserved in vertebrate embryos.
evidence: This is a speculation based on findings from multiple species.

claim: High levels of DLC1 expression are detected in most melanoma tissues.
source: High levels of DLC1 expression are detected in most melanoma tissues, and functional studies have revealed that DLC1 is both necessary and sufficient for melanoma growth and metastasis (Yang et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Yang et al., 2020b.

claim: DLC1 is both necessary and sufficient for melanoma growth and metastasis.
source: High levels of DLC1 expression are detected in most melanoma tissues, and functional studies have revealed that DLC1 is both necessary and sufficient for melanoma growth and metastasis (Yang et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Yang et al., 2020b.

claim: Differences between cranial and trunk NCC delamination have been previously identified.
source: Differences between cranial and trunk NCC delamination have been previously identified.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: In mouse embryos, cranial NCC delaminate from the dorsolateral neuroepithelium or neural plate border prior to neural plate closure.
source: For example, in mouse embryos, cranial NCC delaminate from the dorsolateral neuroepithelium or neural plate border prior to neural plate closure.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about cranial NCC development.

claim: Trunk NCC delaminate from the dorsal neural tube after neural plate closure.
source: Trunk NCC, on the other hand, delaminate from the dorsal neural tube after neural plate closure.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about trunk NCC development.

claim: In the cranial region, premigratory NCC delaminate in bulk as a collective stream.
source: In the cranial region, premigratory NCC delaminate in bulk as a collective stream, to give rise to the cranial ganglia and craniofacial bones and cartilages.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about cranial NCC development.

claim: In the trunk region, premigratory NCC delaminate progressively one after another in a chain migration fashion.
source: In the trunk region, premigratory NCC delaminate progressively one after another in a chain migration fashion to form the sympathetic ganglia, the dorsal root ganglia, glial cells, and melanocytes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about trunk NCC development.

claim: Key signaling pathways and regulatory networks governing cranial and trunk NCC in various species have been shown to differ in these distinct axial populations of NCC.
source: Additionally, key signaling pathways and regulatory networks governing cranial and trunk NCC in various species have also been shown to differ in these distinct axial populations of NCC (Theveneau and Mayor, 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Theveneau and Mayor, 2012.

claim: Intermediate stage cranial NCC during their delamination are consistent with NCC EMT being a developmental EMP event.
source: Taken together, our identification and characterization of intermediate stage cranial NCC during their delamination are consistent with NCC EMT being a developmental EMP event.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: Similar to intermediate EMT states in cancer metastasis, NCC downregulate certain epithelial cell features but maintain co-expression of epithelial cell markers and mesenchymal cell markers during EMT and delamination.
source: Similar to intermediate EMT states in cancer metastasis, NCC downregulate certain epithelial cell features but maintain co-expression of epithelial cell markers and mesenchymal cell markers during EMT and delamination.
evidence: This is a comparison drawn between the findings and cancer EMT.

claim: Intermediate stage NCC are localized at the dorsolateral edge of the neural plate border, which is reminiscent of the localization of intermediate EMT states at the leading edge of invasion in several types of primary tumors.
source: Additionally, intermediate stage NCC are localized at the dorsolateral edge of the neural plate border, which is reminiscent of the localization of intermediate EMT states at the leading edge of invasion in several types of primary tumors.
evidence: This is a comparison drawn between the findings and cancer EMT.

claim: Mouse EMT intermediate NCC represent a transient state and eventually form migratory NCC with mesenchymal character.
source: However, unlike certain intermediate EMT cells present in the lymph nodes or circulating tumor cells, mouse EMT intermediate NCC represent a transient state and eventually form migratory NCC with mesenchymal character.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the trajectory analysis and comparison with cancer EMT.

claim: EMP may be a more common developmental phenomenon.
source: This suggests that EMP may be a more common developmental phenomenon.

source: Furthermore, in vivo time-lapse imaging of chicken embryos revealed that half of the delaminating trunk NCC that were tracked displayed signs of cell division (McKinney et al., 2013).

source: In contrast to delaminating trunk NCC, only around 30% of delaminating cranial NCC in chicken embryos were found to be in S phase (Théveneau et al., 2007) illustrating considerable differences between cranial and trunk NCC and in the correlation between cell cycle phase and delamination.

claim: BMP and Wnt canonical signaling regulates the G1/S transition and promotes trunk NCC delamination.
source: Furthermore, BMP and Wnt canonical signaling regulates the G1/S transition and promotes trunk NCC delamination (Burstyn-Cohen et al., 2004).
